title: Reduction and derived Nakayama
statement:
The finite quotient coefficient has the perfect resolution
$[\mathcal O_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}\mathcal O_{E,X}]$, so $K_n$ is the cone of
$\pi_E^n\colon K\to K$. If a derived-complete complex has $K_1=0$, it is zero.
Consequently a morphism between derived-complete complexes is an isomorphism
whenever its first derived reduction is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the scalar d and the pulled-back short exact sequence of det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution at exponent n+1. Conjugate its first two terms by regularPullbackIso, and identify the quotient map with finiteUnit by faithfulness of the point-module forgetful functor. Form HomologicalComplex.double of this multiplication map in degrees -1 and 0. Its augmentation to the coefficient in degree zero is a quasi-isomorphism: at degree 0, exactness and surjectivity identify the cokernel; at degree -1, injectivity kills the kernel; elsewhere both complexes have zero homology. The two nonzero terms are regular modules, as required. The natural cone identification is the second conclusion of det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution. No ordinary-module perfectness or local strict-perfect package is needed to construct this explicitly specified rank-one resolution.

proof.text: Identify canonical derived scalar extension followed by exact restriction with reductionFunctor at the corresponding positive exponent, using the proved generic residueDerivedTensorIso construction of new-integral-residue-tensor-presentation and the inverse-image compatibility with scalar restriction. Restriction of scalars is faithful and exact, so its derived functor reflects zero objects by its homology comparison. Hence the vanishing of integral first reduction implies the finite-coefficient first reduction vanishes. Apply the vanishing assertion of det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction and retain its IsZero K conclusion.

Use the same natural comparison between restricted scalar extension and tensor reduction. Its naturality transfers invertibility of the tensor-reduction map to invertibility after exact restriction. Restriction reflects isomorphisms on modules and hence on derived categories, using the homology comparison and the homology criterion for invertibility. Apply the isomorphism-detection assertion of det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction.

lean.statement: theorem reduction_and_derived_nakayama (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] : (∃ d : End (Mod.regular (integerRing l E)), (∀ (S : Profinite.{u}ᵒᵖ) (f : (integerRing l E).obj.obj S) (s : S.unop), ((d.hom.hom.app S) f).down s = Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E * f.down s) ∧ ∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (n : ℕ), (∃ (P : CochainComplex (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) ℤ), P.IsStrictlyGE (-1) ∧ P.IsStrictlyLE 0 ∧ ∃ (em : P.X (-1) ≅ Mod.regular (AdicCompletion.ring l E X)) (e0 : P.X 0 ≅ Mod.regular (AdicCompletion.ring l E X)), P.d (-1) 0 = em.hom ≫ (regularPullbackIso l E X).inv ≫ (pullback l E X).map (d ^ (n + 1)) ≫ (regularPullbackIso l E X).hom ≫ e0.inv ∧ ∃ ε : P ⟶ (CochainComplex.singleFunctor (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) 0).obj (AdicCompletion.finiteModule l E X n), QuasiIso ε ∧ ε.f 0 = e0.hom ≫ AdicCompletion.finiteUnit l E X n) ∧ Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ reductionFunctor l E X (n + 1) ≅ coneFunctor l E X (d ^ (n + 1)))) ∧ (∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (K : Derived l E X), IsDerivedComplete l E X K → IsZero ((reductionFunctor l E X 1).obj K) → IsZero K) ∧ (∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (K L : Derived l E X) (f : K ⟶ L), IsDerivedComplete l E X K → IsDerivedComplete l E X L → IsIso ((reductionFunctor l E X 1).map f) → IsIso f)
